subject: Re: Post-call: deployment mode needs (shared vs dedicated) - follow-up

Subject: Post-call recap + next steps — deployment mode (shared vs dedicated)

Sam — thanks again for a productive call today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps. Please ping back if I've missed anything.

Recap of customer needs (from call)
- Workload: high-concurrency inference for customer support summarization and live chat routing (peak ~400 QPS, baseline ~120 QPS).
- Latency SLO: target 200ms p95 for single-turn text generation at 512 tokens.
- Data controls: sensitive PII, preference for strict separation/isolation and audit logging.
- Compliance: SOC 2 required; potential later need for on-prem or VPC deployment for regulated flows.
- Cost sensitivity: want predictable monthly commitment vs variable hosted costs for predictable budget.

Key qualification question we discussed
- Isolation: are you comfortable with Redwood Hosted (shared multi-tenant) if we guarantee isolation boundaries + fallback SLAs, or do you prefer Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pools) or Private VPC/on-prem for full tenancy/isolation?
- Noisy-neighbor tolerance: how much variability in latency under burst load is acceptable?

Proposed next steps
1) Please confirm whether isolation requirements push you toward Dedicated/Private or if you want a written SLA + architectural controls for Hosted.
2) If Dedicated/Private is preferred, confirm expected committed throughput (QPS) and desired failover regions.
3) We'll share our SOC 2 summary and an initial SOW (attached) and schedule a technical deep-dive with our infra engineer (Dev).

Attachments: SOC2-summary.pdf (high-level), initial-sow-draft.pdf (scope/cost ranges)

Happy to jump on another 30-min call this week to go over tradeoffs.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Thanks Priyom — helpful recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Given we process regulated financial messages, isolation is a hard requirement for some customers. Ideally we'd prefer Dedicated capacity for the first phase. If that proves too costly, we can evaluate Private VPC for the most sensitive flows later.
- Noisy neighbor: we need consistent p95 under peak that doesn't exceed 250ms — spikes above that are a risk for SLAs with our customers.
- Throughput: planning for a committed baseline of 150 QPS with headroom to 450 QPS during peak trading hours.

Next actions from Atlas
- We'll review SOW and SOC 2 — circle back with legal for initial redlines.
- Schedule the technical deep-dive with Dev next week (please propose times).

Appreciate the clarity, Sam — that helps a lot. A few quick notes and questions to make the next call efficient: 

1) Dedicated vs Private
- Dedicated capacity gives you tenant isolation at the GPU layer (reserved pools) with predictable throughput and our Dedicated SLAs.
- Private VPC/on-prem provides the strictest network/data isolation but has longer lead time and higher operating overhead.

2) SLO/Noisy neighbor controls we can offer on Dedicated
- Guaranteed baseline throughput with autoscaling policies and burst headroom.
- Per-tenant request shaping and preemptive isolation (we can pin critical workloads to dedicated nodes).
- If we see cross-tenant interference, our fallback is automated routing to standby capacity and dynamic scaling.

Questions for the deep-dive (so Dev can prep):
- Typical request sizes (avg and 95th token length) and expected session affinity (do you keep long-lived KV caches per user?).
- Any on-prem/VPC timing constraints (e.g., must be completed before Q4 launch?).
- Which regions must be supported for failover?

Proposed times for deep-dive (Dev will lead technical architecture + SLO discussion):
- Tue 2026-08-18 10:00-10:45 PT
- Wed 2026-08-19 14:00-14:45 PT

I'll attach the SOC 2 summary and SOW again for reference (see attachments).

Thanks — Priyom

Hi Sam — Dev from Redwood infra here. Short technical notes ahead of the deep-dive: 

1) Noisy neighbor and isolation boundaries
- On Dedicated we provide tenant-aware scheduling: pinned GPU slices for baseline workloads and isolated worker pools for high-priority traffic. That minimizes tail-latency amplification from other tenants.
- We also support KV cache pinning to avoid cold-start token overhead for sessions that need low latency.

2) SLO enforcement and observability
- We can export per-tenant p95/p99 latency metrics, token-level cost breakdowns, and tracing hooks to your observability stack.
- Automatic fallback: if a Dedicated pool degrades, traffic routes to warm standby (another Dedicated pool or compatible hosted instance) depending on your preference. Failover behavior is configurable in rollout policies.

3) Cost/ops note
- Dedicated gives predictable throughput pricing; Private VPC/on-prem provides maximum isolation but requires lead time for networking and key management integration (KMS/HSM).

Prep ask for deep-dive (please reply in-thread with answers):
- Avg tokens per request and 95th percentile tokens
- Average concurrency per session and whether you use long-lived session caches
- Any regulatory timeboxes for Private/VPC completion

Looking forward to the call. If Tue 10:00 PT works for you, I'll send a calendar invite and a short agenda.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Senior Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference

Thanks everyone — Tue 2026-08-18 10:00 PT works for our team. Quick answers to Dev's prep questions below: 

- Avg tokens/request: ~120 tokens; 95th percentile ~640 tokens.
- Concurrency patterns: sessions are short-lived per user but we have many concurrent sessions; affinity is low, so KV caches are per-flow and not long-lived.
- Regulatory timing: we want Dedicated in place for the initial rollout (targeting production by end of Q3). Private VPC is a follow-up for a subset of flows next quarter.

We'll also have two platform engineers join the deep-dive so we can get into network/KMS questions. Looking forward to the calendar invite.

Sam
